findings.title: mcp-ffmpeg-helper handleToolCall command injection

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records OS command injection in sworddut mcp-ffmpeg-helper 0.1.0, 0.1.1, and 0.2.1 through argument handling in src/tools/handlers.ts; the exploit is public and the project had not responded according to the CNA text.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Media-processing MCP helpers can turn agent-selected tool arguments into local command execution when validation is missing.
findings.upstream_routing: Local security lens: agent/tool security and MCP command execution. Broad MCP server catalog ownership remains upstream in ai-wiki.
follow_up_actions: Check whether a maintainer patch appears after the unanswered issue report.
During ingest, consider a local leaf for MCP media helper command-injection boundaries.

findings.title: PraisonAI MCP origin-prefix bypass enables browser-to-local tool calls

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: PraisonAI before 4.6.58 accepted request origins by startswith comparison, allowing attacker-controlled localhost-like origins to match the allowlist and submit MCP tools/call requests to a local server without an API key.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a browser-origin and delegated-tool boundary failure for multi-agent systems reachable from local web contexts.
findings.upstream_routing: PraisonAI as a broad framework/product belongs upstream in ai-wiki; local note should preserve the MCP origin-validation security implication.
follow_up_actions: Group with CVE-2026-55532 during ingest if one PraisonAI origin-validation leaf is created.

findings.title: PraisonAI MCP initialize session exhaustion

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: PraisonAI before 4.6.58 created a new MCP HTTP Stream session for every initialize request without cleanup or a maximum, allowing unauthenticated memory exhaustion; the fix adds cleanup and PRAISONAI_MCP_MAX_SESSIONS.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent runtimes need session lifecycle limits because unauthenticated MCP setup endpoints can become availability attack surfaces.
findings.upstream_routing: PraisonAI entity belongs upstream; local security lens is MCP transport resource exhaustion.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether this belongs with PraisonAI MCP origin issues or a separate MCP session lifecycle control leaf.

findings.title: PraisonAI text/plain MCP CSRF can persist agent instructions

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: PraisonAI before 4.6.58 allowed attacker-controlled localhost.attacker.com origins through prefix matching and accepted text/plain requests without preflight, enabling tools/call without an API key, including file writes that persist agent instructions.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This combines web CSRF/origin mistakes with persistent agent-instruction modification, a concrete autonomous-agent integrity risk.
findings.upstream_routing: PraisonAI general coverage routes upstream; local repo should keep the persistent-instruction and MCP origin-control lesson.
follow_up_actions: Track with browser-to-local MCP threat modeling and instruction-persistence controls.

findings.title: QWED-MCP math verification parse_expr RCE

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: QWED-MCP before 0.2.1 passed attacker-controlled expression strings to SymPy parse_expr without restricted globals or AST validation, enabling arbitrary OS command execution when downstream integrations feed untrusted input to the public library function.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Verification gateways can become pre-execution trust anchors; unsafe expression parsing inside a verifier can compromise the process that is supposed to gate agent actions.
findings.upstream_routing: QWED-MCP as a tool belongs upstream; local security lens is evaluation/verification gateway code execution.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare with QWED core CVE-2026-55585 for shared SymPy parsing guidance.

findings.title: mcp-shell documented default disables command policy

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: mcp-shell before 0.6.0 initialized Security.Enabled to false and the documented bare-binary configuration omitted MCP_SHELL_SEC_CONFIG_FILE, so shell_exec could run unrestricted OS commands as the process user.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Shell MCP servers expose high-impact delegated authority; insecure defaults defeat least privilege for AI-connected command execution.
findings.upstream_routing: mcp-shell entity routes upstream; local repo owns command-approval, least-privilege, and shell-tool policy implications.
follow_up_actions: Consider a local mcp-shell command-policy leaf or update coding-agent command approval boundaries during ingest.

findings.title: mcp-shell Docker bash allowlist bypass

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: mcp-shell before 0.6.0 shipped Docker security.yaml allowing /bin/bash while validation checked only the first token and failed to reject -c, enabling arbitrary commands through shell_exec.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Allowlisting executables is insufficient for agent shell tools unless dangerous interpreter modes and arguments are policy-controlled.
findings.upstream_routing: General package coverage upstream; local security lesson belongs under agent/tool command policy and runtime least privilege.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, fold with other mcp-shell CVEs if maintaining one clustered leaf.

findings.title: mcp-shell Git alias command execution bypass

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: mcp-shell before 0.6.0 allowed /usr/bin/git by default and failed to block Git shell aliases using !, allowing a shell_exec caller to run arbitrary OS commands in the default Docker deployment.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Developer-oriented tools such as Git need argument-level policies when delegated to AI agents, not just executable allowlists.
findings.upstream_routing: mcp-shell package upstream; local route is command argument policy for agent-run developer tools.
follow_up_actions: Track with agent build/dependency execution boundaries and shell-tool hardening.

findings.title: Nextcloud MCP Server unauthenticated webhook vector-index deletion

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Nextcloud MCP Server before 0.117.2 accepted POST /webhooks/nextcloud without authentication when WEBHOOK_SECRET was unset; attacker-controlled user.uid values could delete or re-index Qdrant vector embeddings for any user.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI assistant connectors that mirror user files into vector indexes need authenticated event sources and owner binding to prevent data-integrity loss.
findings.upstream_routing: Nextcloud and MCP server entity context upstream; local security lens is AI connector webhook authentication and vector-store ownership.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, map to data security and MCP data movement exposure controls.

findings.title: browse-mcp arbitrary file write through download and state paths

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: browse-mcp before 0.8.2 let MCP callers control download save_dir and browser state paths, allowing arbitrary file writes; its force_fetch fallback also bypassed the allowed-origin fence. Version 0.8.2 confines paths and honors the origin fence.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser MCP tools bridge untrusted web content, downloads, and local files; prompt-injected agents can turn path arguments into host compromise.
findings.upstream_routing: browse-mcp as a server belongs upstream; local repo owns browser-agent file-boundary and indirect prompt-injection implications.
follow_up_actions: Reconcile with existing browser/agent filesystem containment leaves during ingest.

findings.title: genieacs-mcp DNS rebinding reaches loopback MCP transport

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: genieacs-mcp before 0.3.2 accepted attacker-controlled Host and Origin headers on its default loopback Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint, letting a malicious web page initialize MCP sessions and invoke GenieACS tools through DNS rebinding.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Loopback MCP transports are not inherently browser-safe; Host and Origin validation are required before local automation endpoints accept tool calls.
findings.upstream_routing: GenieACS and the MCP server entity route upstream; local route is browser-origin protection for loopback MCP transports.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, connect to agentic browser intent collision and MCP transport hardening.

findings.title: consciousness-explorer MCP export_state arbitrary file write

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: consciousness-explorer and sublinear-time-solver exposed MCP state/vector file operations that accepted caller-supplied paths without traversal controls; patched releases constrain files to dedicated directories and basename-only inputs.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: State import/export tools in agent-accessible MCP servers need path containment because file writes can become persistence or host-compromise primitives.
findings.upstream_routing: Package/library entity context upstream; local repo owns MCP state tool filesystem containment.
follow_up_actions: Check whether existing agent-tool filesystem containment leaf should absorb this example.

findings.title: Coroot MCP OAuth dynamic client registration redirect hijack

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Coroot accepted arbitrary redirect URIs at its unauthenticated MCP OAuth dynamic client registration endpoint, enabling attackers to register hostile clients, phish signed-in users for consent, capture authorization codes, and exchange them for MCP access tokens.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP OAuth client registration needs redirect URI validation and consent hardening or attackers can hijack delegated agent/tool sessions.
findings.upstream_routing: Coroot product coverage upstream; local route is identity, OAuth, and MCP delegated-authority controls.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare with existing MCP OAuth redirect URI handling leaf.

findings.title: MCP PHP SDK SSE client unbounded memory growth

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: The official MCP PHP SDK versions 0.5.0 through 0.7.0 buffered Server-Sent Events response chunks without an upper bound until a delimiter appeared; malicious or compromised MCP servers could exhaust client memory. Version 0.7.1 fixes it.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Clients need defensive stream limits when connecting agents to untrusted MCP servers; otherwise server-controlled output can deny service to the client process.
findings.upstream_routing: Official SDK context belongs upstream; local repo owns MCP client resilience and tool-output trust boundaries.
follow_up_actions: Route during ingest to MCP transport header/stream hardening or create a client streaming limits note.

findings.title: Kibana AI Assistant conversation ownership bypass

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD records a Kibana authorization bypass where an authenticated user knowing another user's AI Assistant conversation identifier could access or modify that conversation under certain conditions.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI assistant conversation stores need owner-bound identifiers and ACL checks because conversation history can include sensitive operational context.
findings.upstream_routing: Kibana/Elastic product details are upstream-owned; local repo should keep the AI Assistant conversation access-control implication.
follow_up_actions: This resolves the previous run's Kibana date/CVE reconciliation caveat; ingest should check Elastic ESA-2026-51 for fixed versions.

findings.title: QWED verification API SymPy parse_expr RCE

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: QWED before 5.1.2 accepted tenant-supplied math verification expressions and batch jobs that flowed into SymPy parse_expr without sandboxed namespaces, enabling arbitrary Python code execution by any valid tenant API key; default signup could issue such keys.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Security/evaluation platforms for LLM outputs can become multi-tenant execution surfaces when validators evaluate untrusted expressions unsafely.
findings.upstream_routing: QWED product/entity routes upstream; local repo owns security-assurance platform RCE and tenant boundary implications.
follow_up_actions: Compare with CVE-2026-55546 and decide whether one shared deterministic-verification parser-risk leaf is enough.

findings.title: Chainlit unauthenticated MCP stdio command injection

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Chainlit 2.4.0rc0 through before 2.12.0 exposed POST /mcp without authentication when MCP was enabled; stdio transport accepted a user-controlled fullCommand and allowed unchecked arguments, letting npx -c execute arbitrary commands.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Conversational AI app frameworks that expose MCP connection setup can turn unauthenticated HTTP requests into server-side process execution.
findings.upstream_routing: Chainlit framework details route upstream; local security lens is MCP stdio command injection and framework release gates.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, map to hosted MCP server deployment and agent command-approval boundaries.

findings.title: Chainlit MCP SSE and Streamable HTTP SSRF

visible_dates.run_window_basis: NVD published timestamp is inside the 48-hour collection window.

findings.concise_factual_summary: Chainlit 2.4.0rc0 through before 2.12.0 exposed POST /mcp without authentication when MCP was enabled; SSE and Streamable HTTP transport setup accepted arbitrary URLs and headers, allowing blind outbound requests to internal or external services, including metadata endpoints.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent connector setup endpoints need URL allowlists, private-address filtering, and header controls to avoid turning AI app servers into SSRF pivots.
findings.upstream_routing: Chainlit general framework upstream; local route is MCP transport SSRF and cloud-runtime boundary control.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare with existing SSRF leaves for MCP web/browsing/data tools.
